author: Russell Brand
description:
Keir Starmer’s awkward public appearances are treated as more than just personality quirks, pointing instead to a deeper crisis in modern political leadership. The discussion explores why he often appears uncomfortable in classrooms, overly scripted in public settings, and disconnected in everyday interactions, asking whether this reflects media training, institutional pressure, or a wider cultural shift in how leaders are manufactured.
